attempt.description: Runs everything inside the statement, and if something throws an exception (error), the error will not terminate the script. If there is an 'on_error' statement, it will be executed.
attempt.example:
&collection = Coll.Empty
attempt
    Print {Coll.Fetch &collection 2}
end

# The error is handled by on_error when one is present.
on_error with $message
    Print "Handled: {$message}"
end

break.description: Makes a given loop or function (that the 'break' keyword is inside) act as it has completely ended its execution ("breaks" free from the loop/function)
break.example:
# the execution will "break" free after the third iteration
repeat 10 with $iteration
    if {$iteration is 3}
        break
    end
    Print "iteration {$iteration}"
end

chance.description: This statement will execute with the provided chance.

argumentDetails.description: Probability that the body will execute.
argumentDetails.inputDescription: A number from 0 to 1, where 1 is 100%.

chance.example:
chance 25%
    Print "This happens about one time in four."
end

# The chance can also come from a value expression.
$probability = 50%
chance $probability
    Print "This happens about half the time."
end

continue.description: Makes a given loop (that the 'continue' keyword is inside) act as it has reached the end of its body.
continue.example:
# number 3 will be skipped
repeat 5 with $iteration
    if $iteration is 3
        continue
    end
    Print "iteration {$iteration}"
end

argumentDetails.description: Variable to remove from the local or global scope.

over.description: Repeats its body for each player in the player variable or a value in a collection variable, assigning it its own custom variable.

argumentDetails.description: Players or collection whose values are iterated.
argumentDetails.inputDescription: A player value or collection value.

argumentDetails.description: Names variables receiving the current item and optional 1-based index.
argumentDetails.inputDescription: One or two variables compatible with the iterated value.

over.example:
# Run once for every player.
over @all
    Print "found player"
end

# Bind the current item to a temporary variable.
over @all with @plr
    Print "found player {@plr -> name}"
end

# Collections can be iterated in the same way.
&inventory = @sender -> inventory
over &inventory with *item
    Print "found item {*item -> type}"
end

# Add a 1-based index as a second binding.
over @all with @plr $index
    Print "found player #{$index}: {@plr -> name}"
end

# Use break to leave the loop or continue to skip to its next iteration.

repeat.description: Repeats everything inside its body a given amount of times.

argumentDetails.description: Number of times the body should run.
argumentDetails.inputDescription: A non-negative whole-number expression.
A number variable compatible with the loop iteration value.

repeat.example:
# Repeat a fixed number of times.
repeat 10
    Print "hi"
end

# The count can be an expression or variable.
repeat {Random 1 10 int}
    Print "hi"
end

# Bind the current 1-based iteration number.
repeat 10 with $iter
    Print "current iteration: {$iter}"
end

# Use break to leave the loop or continue to skip to its next iteration.

return.description: Returns value when in a function.

argumentDetails.description: Value returned to the caller of the current function.
argumentDetails.inputDescription: Any SER value expression supported by the function's return type.

return.example:

wait.description: Halts execution of the script for a specified amount of time.

argumentDetails.inputDescription: A duration such as 5s, 250ms, or a duration variable.

wait.example:
# Wait for a fixed duration. 
wait 5s

# A duration can also come from a variable.
$duration = 10s
wait $duration

# Or from a random value
$duration = ToDuration {Random 1 10} seconds
wait $duration

wait_until.description: Halts execution of the script until a condition is met.

argumentDetails.description: Expression polled until it evaluates to true.
argumentDetails.inputDescription: A boolean expression; it is evaluated once per frame while waiting.

wait_until.example:
# Wait until the server is empty.
wait_until {AmountOf @all} is 0

# Conditions can use variables and properties too.
wait_until {@sender -> isAlive} is false

while.description: A loop which will execute its body as long as the provided condition is evaluated to true.

argumentDetails.inputDescription: A boolean expression.
A number variable compatible with the loop iteration value.

while.example:
# Check the condition before every iteration.
while {AmountOf @all} > 0
    wait 1s
    Print "there are players on the server!"
end

# Bind the current 1-based iteration number when needed.
while {Chance 90%} with $iter
    Print "current attempt to leave loop: {$iter}"
    wait 1s
end

# Use break to leave the loop or continue to skip to its next iteration.

with.description: This keyword is designed to provide a variable or a collection of variables to a statement.

end

CustomCommand.description:
Creates a command and binds it to the script. When the command is ran, it executes the script. 

Injects the following variables into the script:
> @sender (the player who ran the command, NOT added when command is ran by the server console)
> *command (reference to this 'CustomCommand', used for resetting cooldown)

inlineArgument.name: command name
inlineArgument.description: The name of the command to create

arguments.name: availableFor
arguments.description: Specifies from which console the command can be executed from. Accepts: Player or RemoteAdmin or Server. Defaults to 'server' and 'remoteAdmin'.

arguments.name: requireSender
arguments.description: Makes sure that the @sender variable exists when the command is executed.

arguments.name: description
arguments.description: The description of the command.

arguments.name: neededPermission
arguments.description:
The permission that the player has to have in order to be able to use this command.
You can provide multiple permissions, and if the player has any of the listed permissions, they will be able to use the command.

arguments.name: noPermissionMessage
arguments.description: Defines a message for when the sender does not have the needed permission (defined in 'neededPermission' argument).
arguments.example: -- noPermissionMessage "You do not have the required permissions to ban a player!"

arguments.name: neededRank
arguments.description:
The required remote admin rank in order to have access to this command.
You can provide multiple ranks, and if the player has any of the listed ranks, they will be able to use the command.

arguments.name: invalidRankMessage
arguments.description: Defines a message for when the sender does not have the needed rank (defined in 'neededRank' argument).

arguments.name: cooldown
arguments.description: The time the player has to wait before being able to use the command again.

arguments.name: onCooldownMessage
arguments.description:
Defines a message for when the player tries to run a command but is on cooldown. 
Additionally, you can use %time% in the message to show the remaining time (in seconds) the player has to wait before being able to use the command again.
arguments.example: -- onCooldownMessage "You are on cooldown! You can use this command in %time% seconds."

arguments.name: globalCooldown
arguments.description:
The time all players have to wait before being able to use the command again.
If anyone uses a command, everyone else will be unable to use it for the specified duration.
This also applies to the server console.

arguments.name: onGlobalCooldownMessage
arguments.description:
Defines a message for when someone tries to run a command but is on global cooldown. 
Additionally, you can use %time% in the message to show the remaining time (in seconds) someone has to wait before being able to use the command.
arguments.example: -- onGlobalCooldownMessage "This command is on cooldown! You can use this command in %time% seconds"

arguments.name: maxUses
arguments.description: The maximum number of times a player can use this command.

arguments.name: onMaxUsesMessage
arguments.description: Defines a message for when the player tries to run a command but has reached their maximum usage limit.
arguments.example: -- onMaxUsesMessage "You have already used this command 5 times!"

arguments.name: globalMaxUses
arguments.description: The maximum number of times this command can be used globally.

arguments.name: onGlobalMaxUsesMessage
arguments.description: Defines a message for when the command has reached its global usage limit.
arguments.example: -- onGlobalMaxUsesMessage "This command has reached its global usage limit!"

arguments.name: arguments
arguments.description:
The arguments that this command expects in order to run. 
The script cannot run unless every single argument is specified. 

When the command is ran, the provided values for the arguments turn into their own literal local variables for you to use in the script. 
For example: making a command with an argument 'name' will then create a local variable '$name' in your script.

If you want some arguments to be optional, you can use the '?' symbol after the argument name. 
For example: 'reason?' argument will be optional, and if the sender does not provide a value for it, the script will still run.
Then, the '$reason' command will not be created in your script.

(the '?' suffix is NOT added to the variable names)
